verdict.rationale: Vercel Sandbox documents isolated Linux microVMs that are created programmatically through its SDKs (`@vercel/sandbox`) or with a single CLI command (`sandbox create`), so the one-call provisioning of an isolated environment is clearly delivered. The 'live environment in seconds' part is not evidenced: the docs only say snapshots are 'much faster' than creating from scratch, with no stated boot time. missing for 10: documented or measured startup latency (seconds-level provisioning), independent or hands-on corroboration of create-to-ready speed.

support.subject: As a developer, I can spin up an isolated sandbox with one API/SDK call and get a live environment in seconds

citations.quote: Run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated Linux microVMs.
They provide a programmatic interface to create sandboxes, run commands, and manage files.
Using a snapshot is much faster than creating from scratch because it avoids reinstalling dependencies and repeating setup steps.
